brief: c283: a pane lit before dawn is always an empty room. #190 measured 807 pane-visits a year and took 68 CUT SHORT, 55 LATE and 527 UNSEEN to zero by lifting lampBurn() out of windowLit — but that solved the EVENING burn only. windowLit's other branch, the sunrise-keyed one that lights the early risers, is never offered a paneFigure at all, so the whole first light of every day has lit windows with nobody behind them while the evening has somebody in one pane of six. Give the morning burn the same treatment: paneFigure solves its length inside the MORNING span too, and the early risers get somebody crossing the room.
successLooksLike: Before dawn some of the lit panes have somebody crossing them, and the count of figure-visits a year rises — while the per-evening density #190 tuned (0.98 figures per 10.61 lit-pane-nights, 59/17/9% at 0/1/2) does not move. Quote both against a pinned ref.
avoid: Key the morning on sunUp, never on nightF's span — LAWS: the two axes breathe apart with the season, and a hard-coded hour here is a seasonal bug a screenshot cannot see. And FIG_SHARE 0.16 was hand-tuned at #190 to hold #182's look; adding a second window of visits re-prices the coin, so re-price it rather than letting the evening get busier as a side effect.
